review.summary: The DAG is otherwise executable and correctly routes the R10 work to durable owners: foundation precedes scenario producers, API/Worker implementation scopes are separated from tests, host parity is transitively gated on Panel/network/harness work, and the final gate owns the all-suite/typecheck/build results. The persisted Worker owner-feedback fact is non-blocking and does not create a planning obligation because R10 expressly requires test-injected Worker bindings without a wrangler.local.jsonc deliverable. One browser-harness contract obligation remains unresolved: the declared actual browser producer commands bypass the required pre-load wrapper.

issues.title: Browser test producer verifications bypass the mandatory Playwright pre-load wrapper
issues.detail: R10 requires the unified wrapper to set PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0 before Playwright is first loaded. Although provision_browser_ui_harness promises such a wrapper, the actual verification producers panel_browser_producer and host_parity_browser_producer invoke `npm exec playwright test` directly. That CLI can load Playwright before the planned wrapper runs. The plan also does not concretely bind `test:acceptance` browser-suite dispatch to that wrapper. Thus the sealed project-local Chromium contract is not carried by the actual verification producers for Panel and parity acceptance.
issues.suggestion: Revise the browser producer verification commands to invoke the planned wrapper (for example `node scripts/playwright-acceptance.mjs ...`) rather than `npm exec playwright test` directly, and make the runner's Panel/host-parity/all dispatch explicitly use that same wrapper. Retain the smoke's launch/DOM/external-network-block/clean-close proof. This is a contract-and-DAG correction only; do not require those future browser tests to pass during plan review.

technicalFacts: Spec R10 requires a single wrapper to set PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0 before the first Playwright load.
The plan's panel_browser_producer and host_parity_browser_producer verifications directly execute npm exec playwright test.
A wrapper is only promised in provision_browser_ui_harness.done and is not invoked by those producer verification commands.

finding: Review auto-repair admission checks task targets only. It charged recovery and dispatched a planner even though the requested fix changes verifications outside the declared boundary; submission correctly rejects those verification changes. Root conversational retry limit does not govern the runner automatic recovery policy.

tasks.title: Seed the acceptance-suite command contract
done: Adds root test:acceptance and scripts/test-acceptance.mjs as the earliest ACCEPTANCE-SUITE-RUNNER/R2 source deliverable.
command-contract lists registered suites and rejects an unknown or unregistered suite with non-zero status that names it.
Does not register or invoke a future foundation, API, Worker, Panel, parity, or all producer.

tasks.title: Provision sealed project-local browser UI acceptance harness
done: Sets project-local .npmrc playwright_browsers_path=0 and declares lockfile-pinned, strictly matching @playwright/test and official @playwright/browser-chromium helper versions, so formal dependency preparation installs Chromium at node_modules/playwright-core/.local-browsers for sealed node_modules reuse.
Provides a single wrapper that sets PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0 before importing or loading Playwright, plus deterministic configuration used by Panel and host-parity producers.

Its smoke verification actually launches headless Chromium, loads a local page, asserts DOM content, blocks external network, and cleanly closes the browser; it neither creates a root postinstall nor modifies user npm configuration, caches, standalone browser assets, or node_modules.

decomposition.outcome: Verified sealed local browser UI harness

tasks.title: Build deterministic fixtures, fakes, and redacted evidence producers
done: Creates versioned fake unary and stream transport scenarios that reject undeclared external network access.
Deep-freezes every nested fixture object and array, proving producer mutation cannot alter a shared fixture.

Provides controlled time, random, retry, stream event, authentication, interruption, and write-failure scripts plus evidence redacted for payload, token, session, and txHash in whitespace, nested, and delimiter forms.

tasks.title: Register and revalidate the completed foundation suite
done: Registers only the completed foundation tests producer.
Maps --suite foundation to real assertions and retains named non-zero unknown-suite behavior.
Revalidates command-contract and foundation through the public runner.

decomposition.outcome: Foundation suite available through public runner

tasks.title: Add local fake transport injection to API protocol service
done: Adds explicit test-only injection at the consoCall/consoStream transport boundary while retaining production routing/defaults.
Preserves payload isolation, endpoint compatibility, missing-auth and terminal 401-after-refresh behavior, and controlled interruption/reconnection.
Keeps acceptance paths away from real credentials, wallet connections, signing, and broadcasts.

tasks.title: Preserve Worker route gates under local fake routing
done: Adds explicit Worker-scoped local-test routing/adaptation while preserving normal method, path, family, AuthV2, CORS, upgrade, and proxy gates.
Fake handling cannot access an external upstream and does not alter deployment or user configuration.
Uses test-injected Worker bindings rather than writing wrangler.local.jsonc, which remains outside this task's required deliverable.

tasks.title: Produce API and Worker behavioral contract scenarios
done: Adds real API and Worker suite producers using the completed deterministic foundation.
Covers unary/stream, anonymous and terminal-401 behavior, disconnect/backoff/reconnect/eventual error, valid fake, unauthorized, invalid method/path/family, CORS, upgrade, and no-upstream cases.
Verifies local-only behavior with no sensitive evidence, wallet connection, signing, or broadcast.

decomposition.outcome: Fixed local API and Worker behavioral evidence

tasks.title: Register and revalidate completed API and Worker suites
done: Registers only completed API and Worker producers after foundation.
Maps each suite to actual tests and preserves command-contract failure semantics.
Reexecutes foundation, API, and Worker suites after this runner change.

tasks.title: Add shared Panel test seams and stable semantics
done: Adds minimal injection seams and stable roles, labels, or test identifiers to the existing shared Panel without duplicating product views.
Connects Market, Search, Detail Chart/Data/Holders/Profit/Trades, Watchlist, and Trade to completed fake transport contracts while preserving production defaults.
Supports deterministic Watchlist rollback/retry/local-order submission and no-wallet Trade quote, allowance, preflight, approve/swap/submission/status branches.

decomposition.outcome: Testable shared Panel with compatible production behavior

tasks.title: Produce browser-executed shared Panel journeys
done: Uses the verified browser harness to mount the existing shared Panel with fixture-injected local page/float adapters and stable semantic selectors.

Adds authenticated-market, search-detail, watchlist-recovery, trade-simulation, and auth-and-network-failures assertions covering lists, search, all Detail views/periods, rollback/retry/order submission, and Trade success/rejection/timeout/failure/retry.
Performs no real network, credential, wallet, signing, or broadcast action.

tasks.title: Register and revalidate completed Panel journeys
done: Registers the completed browser Panel producer only after it exists.
Maps --suite panel to the real browser assertions.
Reexecutes all registered consumer suites after runner modification.

decomposition.outcome: Panel suite available through public runner

Uses PanelApp page mode rather than a parallel product implementation.

Revalidates Panel and network behavior through both hosts without real network, credentials, wallet connection, signing, or broadcast.

review.summary: The DAG is otherwise executable and correctly stages test producers before suite registration without requiring future test results at plan time. However, the actual browser producer verification commands bypass the mandated pre-load wrapper, leaving the R10 sealed-browser contract unresolved.

issues.title: Browser verification producers invoke Playwright without the required pre-load wrapper
issues.detail: The frozen R10 Spec/Ticket requires the single wrapper to set PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0 before Playwright is first loaded, and requires browser-suite dispatch through that wrapper. The executable verification definitions for panel_browser_producer and host_parity_browser_producer instead run `npm exec playwright test ...` directly. Those commands may load Playwright before `scripts/playwright-acceptance.mjs` can set the environment. The task.done claims that later runner dispatch will use the wrapper, but the concrete verification producers are the controlling execution contracts and do not do so. This remains a planning-contract defect, not a request that future browser tests pass now.
issues.suggestion: Change panel_browser_producer and host_parity_browser_producer to invoke the planned wrapper directly (for example, `node scripts/playwright-acceptance.mjs ...`), with that wrapper forwarding the acceptance config and test path. Keep the runner’s panel, host-parity, and all dispatch explicitly bound to the same wrapper, and retain the separate actual-launch smoke verification. Do not add a plan-review requirement to execute these future tests before their producer tasks run.

technicalFacts: Spec R10 mandates that the unified wrapper set PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0 before first loading Playwright.
The plan's panel_browser_producer and host_parity_browser_producer verification commands directly execute `npm exec playwright test`.
The workspace currently has neither a scripts/*playwright* harness file nor a tests/** tree; these are planned outputs, so no current execution pass is required for this review.
